name: Causal attribution

subjectOf.text: If corporate wrongdoing is not in fact caused by deficient corporate governance, then the governance reform imposed through a non or deferred prosecution agreement is merely a method of settlement rather than a lasting reform effort.
subjectOf.abstract: If corporate wrongdo- ing is not the result of lacking corporate governance, it seems possible that N/DPA related governance reform is just a method of settlement rather than a lasting re- form effort.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Timothy Lacine, The Effect of Deferred and Non-Prosecution Agreements on Corporate Governance Evidence from 1993-20 (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2486570
scope_conditions: holds where the wrongdoing has no identifiable governance cause

subjectOf.text: Among the minority of respondents who believed Dodd-Frank affected fund earnings, the majority attributed that effect to additional compliance costs rather than to lower returns.
subjectOf.abstract: Figure 17 illustrates that the majority of those respondents who believed that Dodd-Frank affected their fund(s) earnings blamed additional compliance costs associated with Dodd-Frank.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: respondents who answered yes to survey question 11

subjectOf.text: Madoff related cases following the discovery of the Ponzi scheme in 2008 only partially explain the significant increase in the prevalence and importance of private fund investor due diligence after 2009.
subjectOf.abstract: Madoff-related cases in the aftermath of the discovery of the Madoff Ponzi scheme in 2008 only partially explain the significant increase in the prevalence and importance of private fund IDD after 2009.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Investor Due Diligence – Evidence from 1995 to 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2811718
